title: Roadstorm TacticalIntent record (intent schema version 1)
description: Machine-readable contract for the TacticalIntent that a Classic planner or a Roadstormer policy produces and the shared safety layer and path follower consume (docs/OPPONENT_AI.md 'Architecture' steps 2-4; the 'AIObservation/TacticalIntent' row of docs/TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md 'Content contracts': version, ordered shape/fields, road frame, masks, observation age, normalization/action decoding, personality/difficulty and reset defaults, defined before M4.2). This is a text contract defined at M0.9. It requires no working AI implementation and defines no model, weights, export, training or inference interface; those are ratified separately at M4B and are deliberately absent here. Every field, bound, age rule and reset rule below restates semantics specified in docs/OPPONENT_AI.md; values that document leaves undetermined are null in instances and MUST be listed in the enclosing fixture's 'unknowns' (see intent_fixture.schema.json). Revision 1.1.0 (M0.9 independent schema checkpoint, 2026-11-27) records the checkpoint's required changes before the M2.7 ratification: the proposed decode and the executed state are now separate members (commitment.executed_label, commitment.commit_started_tick, drift.executed_preference), the pace interval and decoded target are tied together, speed corrections are nonnegative and checked against the pre-safety decode, and tick-level safety exposure plus emergency substitution/fallback telemetry have a defined home (safety.interventions, safety.emergency).

schema_version.description: Contract revision. A record whose schema_version differs is rejected, not silently migrated; a contract change requires a new version and a recorded decision. 1.0.0 was the initial M0.9 draft; 1.1.0 is the revision taken at the independent M0.9 schema checkpoint (2026-11-27) that split the proposed decode from the executed state and added the pace-decode, tick-intervention and emergency-telemetry rules; the decision is recorded in fixtures/intent/README.md.

intent_layout_revision.description: Field-order/layout revision of this contract, parallel to observation_layout_revision in schemas/observation/observation_record.schema.json (the accepted 'Shared schema version 1' observation contract).

intent_id.description: Stable ID of this intent record, e.g. intent.surge_commit.t000996. Two records are two distinct proposals and must not share an ID: BENCHMARKS.md 'AI metrics' counts material corrections and emergency replacements once per proposed 5 Hz intent by this identity. Within a fixture every record's ID is unique; a deployed capture stream must keep the same uniqueness across every intent it counts together (the cross-run scope is not further specified).

source_observation_id.description: ID of the observation record this intent was computed from, as defined by schemas/observation/observation_record.schema.json (observation_id). The intent never observes more than that contract allows. A resolvable source's sampled_tick may not follow this record's generated_tick, and must not lag it by a full 5 Hz sampling period (delay < 12 ticks at 60 Hz): GAME_DESIGN documents 0-200 ms of sub-period 5 Hz planning phase latency on top of the traffic observation age, while this slice treats an intent age at or beyond one period as a missed update. The source must therefore be the current tactical sample; exact observation-to-decision synchrony is not specified, so equality is deliberately not required. traffic_age_ticks remains the source snapshot's age and any sub-period delay is additional reaction latency that BENCHMARKS reports as observed end-to-intent latency.

kind.description: Which producer emitted the intent: authored Classic rules, the behavioral-cloning-only Roadstormer policy, or the PPO-trained Roadstormer learned tactical policy. All three emit this same contract; OPPONENT_AI.md requires Classic planners to emit the shared intent from M4.2 onward. cloning_only_policy is the teacher-initialized policy that OPPONENT_AI.md ('Training approach') and docs/BENCHMARKS.md ('Tactical comparison') require to be evaluated separately from the PPO-trained policy, and it is the same driver kind schemas/scenario/scenario.schema.json's participant driver enum already names; the two producers are distinguished by producer_revision, never by an undocumented convention.

producer_revision.description: Revision of the producing code/configuration, recorded like handling_fixture.schema.json's controller_revision: a producer change is a dependency change recorded before reruns. A placeholder string is acceptable only while the real revision is unratified and listed in the fixture unknowns.

difficulty.description: Explicit difficulty input. Selects the delayed traffic age (18/12/7 ticks) and the desired speed-profile interval used to decode pace.

style.description: Explicit style input. 'surge'/'switch' are the two learned styles; 'none' is the Classic-only style input pair 0/0 (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Shared schema version 1').

road_frame.description: Route frame is forward tangent, right lateral, up road normal; positive lane offset is right (same convention as schemas/observation/observation_record.schema.json). The strings name the frame's axes; concrete vectors are runtime state, not frozen here.

generated_tick.description: 60 Hz simulation tick at which the planner emitted this intent. Tactical decisions run at 5 Hz, so consecutive intents for one participant are 12 ticks apart.

sampled_tick.description: 60 Hz tick at which this record was exported for telemetry/demonstration. intent_age_ticks = sampled_tick - generated_tick.

intent_age_ticks.description: Age of this intent at sampled_tick, in 60 Hz ticks. Fresh intents are re-issued every 12 ticks (5 Hz); an age at or beyond the 12-tick staleness threshold means a missed tactical update. The required behavior for a stale intent (hold, decay, fall back) is not specified by OPPONENT_AI.md and is unratified; see the fixture unknowns.

traffic_age_ticks.description: Age of the delayed traffic snapshot this intent was computed from, inherited from the source observation: Rookie 18, Racer 12, Expert 7 ticks at 60 Hz (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Shared schema version 1'). Ego/road data and the emergency guard remain current; only traffic-derived data is delayed.

tactical_rate_hz.description: Tactical decision rate. OPPONENT_AI.md specifies 'initially' 5 Hz; changing it requires a new schema_version and a recorded decision.

period_ticks.description: Sampling period in 60 Hz ticks (5 Hz).

period_s.description: Sampling period in seconds. A held tactical intent never suspends hazard checks for this long.

lateral_target_norm.description: Preferred lane/offset as the continuous proposed value (action 0 of the shared action contract), positive right. The planner proposes; the safety layer may correct.

legal_corridor_half_width_m.description: Half-width of the legal lateral corridor used to decode the target: (road_width - car_width)/2 - 0.5 m. null when the record does not fix road/car width; a null requires a matching unknowns entry.

decoded_offset_m.description: Decoded/executed lateral target in meters after the safety layer: lateral_target_norm times the corridor half-width, bounded to the legal corridor. Recorded separately from the proposed normalized value, as OPPONENT_AI.md requires ('Record the proposed intent, ordinary difficulty decoding, safety changes and final commands separately'). null when the record does not fix road/car width; a null requires a matching unknowns entry.

pace_norm.description: Target pace within the safe envelope: (action 1 + 1)/2 mapped into the selected difficulty's desired speed-profile interval, before safety counting.

speed_profile_interval_m_s.description: The difficulty's desired speed-profile interval the pace decodes into, in m/s. The interval is ordered: min <= max (an inverted interval is rejected semantically, because JSON Schema cannot compare two members of one object). The per-difficulty intervals are tuned at M4.3 and are not numerically specified by OPPONENT_AI.md, so this is null until ratified; a null requires a matching unknowns entry and forbids a determined target_speed_m_s and any pace correction.

target_speed_m_s.description: Decoded target speed in m/s after the safety layer, recorded separately from the proposed pace_norm as OPPONENT_AI.md requires ('Record the proposed intent, ordinary difficulty decoding, safety changes and final commands separately'). When no pace correction exists it equals the pre-safety decode min + pace_norm x (max - min) of the interval above; when a pace correction exists it equals that correction's applied value. null until the speed-profile intervals are ratified; a null requires a matching unknowns entry.

commitment_raw.description: Follow/pass commitment as the continuous proposed value (action 2 of the shared action contract).

label.description: Decoded commitment: below -1/3 follow, -1/3 through +1/3 wait/hold, above +1/3 commit to a legal pass. The wait band includes both thresholds. This is the pure threshold decode of the proposed commitment_raw and may differ from the executed state below while a commitment is held.

executed_label.description: The decoded/executed commitment the safety layer and path follower actually ran, recorded separately from the proposed decode in 'label' (OPPONENT_AI.md: 'Record the proposed intent, ordinary difficulty decoding, safety changes and final commands separately'). A commitment that starts at a record must match that record's proposed decode; afterwards the executed label stays commit_pass for at least min_commitment_s (0.4 s = 24 ticks at 60 Hz) even when the proposal has moved back into the wait band, and only a hazard interruption may end it earlier.

commit_started_tick.description: 60 Hz tick at which the executing commit_pass began; it equals the generated_tick of the intent that started the commitment. Non-null exactly when executed_label is commit_pass, and null (not applicable, not undetermined) otherwise.

min_commitment_s.description: Minimum commitment duration in seconds for a pass commitment, interrupted by hazards (OPPONENT_AI.md action table).

hold_window_s.description: Length of the short anti-jitter commitment window held around the label. OPPONENT_AI.md requires holding 'a short commitment window' but does not fix its length, so this is null until ratified; a null requires a matching unknowns entry.

interrupted.description: true when a hazard interrupted the held commitment. A held tactical intent never suspends hazard checks. An interruption is the only reason an executing commit_pass may lapse before the 0.4 s minimum.

interruption_reason.description: The hazard that interrupted or overrode the held commitment. Required non-null when interrupted is true; null when interrupted is false.

drift_raw.description: Drift preference as the continuous proposed value (action 3 of the shared action contract).

label.description: Decoded drift preference: above +0.25 drift, below -0.25 grip, retain the preference between thresholds. The follower still enforces legal drift entry conditions; the label never grants them. 'retain' is the decode band, not the preference actually retained; executed_preference carries that.

executed_preference.description: The executed drift preference after 'retain' is resolved: drift or grip when the label decodes outside the retain band, the retained prior preference while inside it, and 'none' when retain has no prior preference to keep because the reset masked the history (reset.history_valid 0 / post_reset_defaults_applied). The follower still enforces legal entry conditions; this value never grants them.

enabled.description: Intents are interpolated between 5 Hz decisions to prevent jitter and lane weaving (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Architecture').

window_s.description: Interpolation window, equal to the 5 Hz sampling period.

curve.description: Interpolation curve identifier. OPPONENT_AI.md does not specify the curve, so this is null until ratified; a null requires a matching unknowns entry.

max_deferral_ticks.description: Immediate hazard safety never waits for the delayed traffic snapshot or the 0.2 s tactical period: a held intent never suspends hazard checks, so the safety layer may defer hazard checks by zero ticks.

corrections.description: Safety-layer changes to the proposed intent, one entry per corrected field. The safety layer constrains the intent to the road, available passing room, contact rules and physical capability (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Architecture' step 3). Empty when the proposal was already legal. A correction belongs to this 5 Hz intent and is counted once per intent by intent identity (BENCHMARKS.md 'AI metrics'); the tick-level exposure of per-tick safety lives in interventions, and wholesale replacement lives in emergency.

ticks.description: Ascending, distinct 60 Hz ticks inside this intent's hold window [generated_tick, generated_tick + sampling.period_ticks) at which the immediate per-tick safety layer replaced or overrode the intent's commands. BENCHMARKS.md counts one intent corrected on several 60 Hz ticks once (by intent identity) and reports tick-level exposure beside that count; this array is that exposure. Empty when per-tick safety never overrode the held intent.

interventions.description: Tick-level safety exposure for this intent. Immediate hazard safety runs at every 60 Hz simulation tick (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Architecture'), so overrides can happen between the 5 Hz decisions; recording their ticks keeps the per-tick and per-intent views reconcilable without duplicating the intent identity used for 5 Hz deduplication.

substituted.description: true when the safety layer replaced the proposed intent wholesale instead of correcting a field: the emergency substitution/reset and the safe-Classic fallback that OPPONENT_AI.md counts separately from ordinary corrections ('emergency substitution/reset is separate'; 'Invalid output or missing weights triggers a visible diagnostic and safe Classic control').

kind.description: Which replacement ran: an emergency stop/reset substitution, or a safe Classic control fallback for a learned/cloning-only producer (persistent replacement by Classic counts as a learned failure per BENCHMARKS.md). Non-null exactly when substituted is true. The kind vocabulary is provisional until the intervention categories are preregistered before evaluation (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Implementation and acceptance'); see the fixture unknowns.

tick.description: 60 Hz tick inside this intent's hold window at which the substitution took effect for this intent; for a persistent substitution it is the tick inside the current window, not the original one. Non-null exactly when substituted is true.

persistent.description: true when this substitution continues the same-kind substitution of the immediately preceding intent of this participant (a run of substitutions, such as a stuck Classic fallback). false for a fresh substitution and whenever nothing is substituted.

reason.description: The fault or hazard that forced the replacement. Required non-null when substituted is true; null when substituted is false.

reset_generation.description: Counts participant resets/recoveries. Reset restores timers, counters, history, contact/recovery state and queued events (OPPONENT_AI.md 'Training approach'; TECHNICAL_DESIGN fixed-tick reset), so the generation makes intent history comparable across resets.

history_valid.description: 1 when pass/occupancy/contact history feeding this intent is valid; 0 when it is masked to zero/default after a reset, mirroring the observation masks ('Preserve feature timestamps and reset history to zero/masked defaults').

post_reset_defaults_applied.description: true when this intent was produced after a reset with default history substituted.

defaults_applied.description: Dotted field names reverted to defaults after the reset.

constants.description: Single source of truth for the numeric semantics of this contract, all from docs/OPPONENT_AI.md. The fixtures/intent validator reads these instead of restating them.

intent_staleness_ticks.description: An intent at or beyond this age marks a missed 5 Hz update; the required stale-intent behavior is unratified.

commitment_min_ticks.description: The 0.4 s minimum commitment expressed in 60 Hz ticks (0.4 x 60). An executing commit_pass may not lapse before this many ticks unless a hazard interrupted it.

safety_check_period_ticks.description: Immediate hazard safety runs at every 60 Hz simulation tick, so the safety layer's per-tick override cadence is one tick; the 5 Hz tactical intent never suspends it.

lateral_margin_m.description: Lateral decode: target times (road_width - car_width)/2 - 0.5 m.

material_lane_change_car_widths.description: BENCHMARKS.md 'AI metrics': a safety-caused lane change greater than 0.1 car widths is material.

material_speed_change_fraction.description: BENCHMARKS.md 'AI metrics': abs(safe - proposed) / max(proposed, 1 m/s) greater than 0.05 is material.

action_decoding.description: The shared action contract (one continuous Box vector of four values in [-1,1]) and its decoding into this intent, restated from OPPONENT_AI.md 'Shared schema version 1'. It is documented here as decoding only; the model/export interface that produces the vector is ratified at M4B and is not part of this contract.

allOf.description: A speed target cannot be negative, so a pace.target_speed_m_s correction carries nonnegative proposed/applied values. The intent slice's JSON Schema subset does not evaluate allOf/if/then, so fixtures/intent/validate_intent_contract.py enforces the same rule semantically (pace_decode_consistency); a full draft 2020-12 validator rejects it at the schema layer.

field.description: Intent field the safety layer corrected. Commitment interruption is recorded on commitment.interrupted, not as a correction.

category.description: Which constraint forced the change; the safety layer constrains the intent to the road, available passing room, contact rules and physical capability.

proposed.description: Pre-safety decoded value in the field's units: for lateral, lateral_target_norm times the corridor half-width; for pace, min + pace_norm x (max - min) of the speed-profile interval. A pace correction with a negative proposed value is invalid.

applied.description: Post-safety value actually handed to the path follower. A pace correction with a negative applied value is invalid.

material.description: Whether the change is material per BENCHMARKS.md: lateral change greater than 0.1 car widths, or speed-target change abs(applied - proposed) / max(proposed, 1 m/s) greater than 0.05, in either direction.
